verses.before: ‘Say to Joseph, “Please forgive the transgression of your brothers and their sin, because they did evil to you.”’ And now, please forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of your father.” Joseph wept when they spoke to him.
verses.after: ‘Tell Joseph, “Please forgive your brothers’ offense and sin, for they did you harm.”’ Now please forgive the offense of the servants of your father’s God.” Joseph wept when their message reached him.
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Say to Joseph, “Please forgive the transgression of your brothers and their sin, because they did evil to you.”’ And now, please forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of your father.” Joseph wept when they spoke to him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the actual bow and offer of slavery, allowing the dream echo without inserting commentary into the verse.
verses.before: His brothers also came and fell down before him and said, “Look, we are your servants.”
verses.after: His brothers also came, fell down before him, and said, “Here we are, your slaves.”
verses.tsw_comparator: His brothers also came and fell down before him and said, “Behold, we are your servants.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the rhetorical question and reassurance rather than turning Joseph’s response into an abstract doctrine.
verses.before: Yet Joseph said to them, “Do not fear, for am I in the place of God?
verses.after: But Joseph told them, “Do not be afraid. Am I in God’s place?
verses.tsw_comparator: But Joseph said to them, “Do not fear, for am I in the place of God?

verses.rationale: Repeats intended for both agents while preserving the contrast between human harm and divine good and its stated life-preserving outcome.
verses.before: As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to bring it about that many people should be kept alive, as they are today.
verses.after: You intended harm against me; God intended it for good, to bring about what is happening today: keeping many people alive.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to bring it about that many people should be kept alive, as they are today.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated reassurance, emphatic personal provision, explicit children, and heart idiom linked to comfort.
verses.before: So do not fear; I will provide for you and your little ones.” Thus he comforted them and spoke to their hearts.
verses.after: So do not be afraid. I myself will provide for you and your little ones.” He comforted them and spoke to their hearts.
verses.tsw_comparator: So do not fear; I will provide for you and your little ones.” Thus he comforted them and spoke to their hearts.

verses.rationale: Keeps place and household together and states the exact lifespan without an added ideal-age explanation.
verses.before: So Joseph remained in Egypt, he and his father’s house. Joseph lived 110 years.
verses.after: Joseph remained in Egypt with his father’s household. He lived a hundred and ten years.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Joseph remained in Egypt, he and his father’s house. Joseph lived 110 years.

verses.rationale: Preserves the generation expression and knee image without inventing an obstetric practice or silently reducing it to generic survival.
verses.before: Joseph saw Ephraim’s children of the third generation. The children also of Machir the son of Manasseh were counted as Joseph’s own.
verses.after: Joseph saw Ephraim’s descendants to the third generation. The children of Machir, Manasseh’s son, were also born on Joseph’s knees.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Joseph saw Ephraim’s children of the third generation. The children also of Machir the son of Manasseh were counted as Joseph’s own.

verses.rationale: Renders emphatic visit as effective aid, retaining ascent, the oath, and all three ancestors in source order.
verses.before: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am about to die, but God will surely visit you and bring you up out of this land to the land that he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.”
verses.after: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am about to die. But God will surely come to your aid and bring you up from this land to the land he swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Joseph said to his brothers, “I am about to die, but God will surely visit you and bring you up out of this land to the land that he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.”

verses.rationale: Repeats the assurance exactly and preserves the oath and bones rather than replacing them with a general burial wish.
verses.before: Then Joseph made the sons of Israel swear, saying, “God will surely visit you, and you will carry up my bones from here.”
verses.after: Then Joseph made the Israelites swear an oath: “God will surely come to your aid. When he does, carry my bones up from here.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joseph made the sons of Israel swear, saying, “God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from here.”

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated age, embalming, coffin, and final Egypt location without resolving the book’s unfinished return.
verses.before: So Joseph died, being 110 years old. They embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.
verses.after: Joseph died at a hundred and ten years old. They embalmed him and placed him in a coffin in Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Joseph died, being 110 years old. They embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.
